scope: Independent standard for pca9685 on the fixed i2c task configuration, based on its copied reference driver, fixed task requirements, supplied Zephyr API pack and harness. Excludes sample_ref application cadence and device-register behavior.

api_contract.fixed_task_context: i2c1 DT device handle and 7-bit target address

signatures.i2c_burst_read: int i2c_burst_read(const struct device *dev, uint16_t addr, uint8_t start_addr, uint8_t *buf, uint32_t num_bytes)
signatures.i2c_burst_write: int i2c_burst_write(const struct device *dev, uint16_t addr, uint8_t start_addr, const uint8_t *buf, uint32_t num_bytes)

headers: zephyr/kernel.h for timing calls where used
api_contract.return_semantics: Use the integer status from fallible bus/configuration calls; GPIO read yields level or error. UART poll_in is nonblocking: 0 means byte received, nonzero means no byte; poll_out returns void.
api_contract.timing_semantics: The driver calls k_busy_wait(500) after oscillator wake; the device note specifies up to 500 us for oscillator startup, so software needs to ensure at least this settling duration. A longer delay (for example 1 ms) is semantically acceptable if the delay API is available in this Zephyr task.

facts.requirement: Bind the required i2c handle/configuration on fixed task context: i2c1 DT device handle and 7-bit target address.

Provide the task-required operations with compatible signatures: int i2c_burst_read(const struct device *dev, uint16_t addr, uint8_t start_addr, uint8_t *buf, uint32_t num_bytes); int i2c_burst_write(const struct device *dev, uint16_t addr, uint8_t start_addr, const uint8_t *buf, uint32_t num_bytes); void k_busy_wait(uint32_t us). Keep handle/address/configuration, buffer and return levels compatible with the reference.

After waking the PCA9685 oscillator, ensure at least 500 microseconds of settling time as in the reference. This is a device minimum wait, not a software maximum; longer waits are acceptable. Equivalent RTOS timing APIs are allowed when their availability in the task can be established.
Preserve the fallible API status needed to detect or propagate bus/GPIO configuration and transaction failures; do not convert an error return into success.
